newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK brokers bolster China teams, play musical chairs.
newsitem.headline: HK brokers bolster China teams, play musical chairs.

text.p: Strong demand for China-related stocks has prompted a competitive game of musical chairs in Hong Kong's brokerage industry as firms vie to bolster their China research and secure the best teams, analysts said on Friday.

"We have been expanding since last year. We started with one (China analyst) last year and since then we have brought on board a whole new team," said An Lu, vice president at Salomon Brothers. "We continue to look for people."
Lu joined Salomon Brothers last July from Nomura Research.
Salomon has about seven analysts covering China stocks and recently hired Allen Huie from Vickers Ballas as managing director in charge of Greater China investment banking coverage.
At Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, the China research team is expanding at a faster rate than other departments.

Head of China research Lawrence Ang said the firm had hired Theresa Low, previously from Kim Eng Securities, about two months ago and Vincent Cheng from New World Development Co Ltd last week to bring its China research team to five.
Ang joined Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in February from a similar position at BZW Asia.

"We have something like two to three new companies listing in Hong Kong every month and even Hong Kong-based companies are increasingly expanding their China exposure," said Ang. "To analyse these companies now you need good China analysts."
Turnover in red chips and H-shares has trounced volume in Hong Kong's blue-chip stocks in some recent sessions due to a growing appetite for exposure to China's expanding economy.
Red chips are Hong Kong-incorporated companies with financial backing from China and H-shares are stocks of mainland-incorporated companies listed in Hong Kong.
"I don't rule out the possibility (of expansion) as the asset class of H-shares and red chips expands," said Keith Wu, head of Hong Kong and China research at Peregrine Brokerage.
Peregrine has about six China analysts in Hong Kong. Chen Xing Dong, previously from SocGen-Crosby Securities, is due to start as Peregrine's China economist in Beijing next week.
Institutional Investor ranked Credit Lyonnais' team as the top China research team in the region in its annual All Asia Research Team survey in April, with Jardine Fleming coming in second place.
But in their efforts to expand their teams, brokerage firms said they were finding good China analysts hard to come by.

"There is an undersupply," said Li Hui, senior analyst at W.I. Carr. "There is a lack of experience and in the China market you need to speak Mandarin and English very well. Financial knowledge is also very important," she said.
Li joined the firm in September 1996 from G.K. Goh Securities. Two more analysts will be joining the current team of four China analysts at the end of the month, she said.
Analysts said China's emerging market was different than Hong Kong's property and banking dominated market since it required more knowledge of heavy industry, trading and conglomerates.
"The market is quite unique. It requires a lot of local knowledge, a lot of local contacts, to be able to get close to companies and understand how the Chinese do business," said Au.
But analysts said Hong Kong and China research teams should eventually come together as the handover of the territory to Chinese rule on July 1 influences Hong Kong's economy.
"The economies are integrating, the countries are integrating and naturally the stock markets will integrate," said Chong Leong, China analyst at ING Barings.
